span.span: Common guard. APS and DSD append the following constraints: “Never quote, paraphrase, or retell what is being said—not the words, events, actions, names, or plot; and never use quotation marks. Judge the voice by its SOUND (pitch, pace, volume, energy, timbre), NOT by the meaning of the words—as if you did not understand the language. Describe only the human voice (not background sounds or audio quality). State the volume exactly as the tag says (loud / moderate / soft)—an energetic or fast delivery is not the same as loud volume.” Free form additionally requires a plausible, general role and scene rather than specific content inferred from the words. In text-only mode, its content rule instead says the transcript may inform only the general register and setting; acoustic claims must come from tags. RP uses a separate rule that forbids deriving its role or scene from topic, plot, events, or meaning and requires every concrete attribute it mentions to match its tag. All forms describe standard Mandarin without calling it an accent.

Format examples. The APS format example is “Male, 40–55 years old; low-pitched, deep timbre; measured pace, moderate volume; standard Mandarin.” The DSD example is “A deep, resonant voice at a medium pitch, delivered at a steady, measured pace and a moderate volume, with a calm and composed emotional undertone that conveys a mature, steady, and responsible character.” RP rotates one of six role-and-scene examples; each prompt instructs the captioner to invent its own imagery rather than copy the example. Chinese prompts use corresponding Chinese task and constraint text.
